about:
Wilcox Family Farms is headquartered in Great Falls, Montana, and operates a 1,600-acre egg farm along the Nisqually River in the foothills of Mount Rainier, Washington. The business was founded in 1909 by Judson and Elizabeth Wilcox and remains family-owned, now in its fourth generation under brothers Andy, Brent, and Chris Wilcox.

The farm raises Certified Humane hens and produces shell eggs for food-service, retail, and wholesale channels. Operations cover layer-hen management, egg collection, grading, packing, and distribution across the Pacific Northwest. The 1,600-acre property provides pasture access for the flock, and the company emphasizes sustainable land stewardship.

Wilcox supplies eggs to restaurants, institutional food-service distributors, grocery retailers, and local pantries throughout the Pacific Northwest. Its food-service line serves commercial kitchens, while retail products reach consumer shelves under the Wilcox Family Farms brand.

The Wilcox family states that the farm was built on a commitment to animal welfare and land conservation, with a goal of keeping the operation honest, sustainable, and close to home for the next century. Certification by Certified Humane underscores the welfare standards applied to every hen.
